brief.summary: An analysis workspace used by a university nonprofit-studies research group to examine program data that partner nonprofits share under data-use agreements.
brief.user: Dr. Hana Kowalczyk, a postdoctoral researcher in a public policy school's Nonprofit Effectiveness Lab. She is comfortable with statistics and has spent four months with this dataset, preparing findings for the partner organization's national board.
brief.moment: The partner, a national youth mentoring nonprofit, saw volunteer mentor retention drop from 71% to 58% in 2025, mostly in some regions. Hana's working hypothesis is that a 2024 cut to pre-match training hours lowered retention. A colleague thinks it's caused by longer waits between mentor sign-up and being matched with a child. She is breaking retention down by chapter, training hours, and wait-to-match days, picking out the chapters that don't fit either explanation, and deciding which pattern holds up well enough to present at Tuesday's lab meeting.
brief.data: 18,412 de-identified mentor records from 212 chapters across 9 regions, 2021–2025. Fields: chapter ID, region, chapter size, mentor sign-up date, training hours completed (range 2–14), days from sign-up to match (median 47, range 3–310), match start/end dates, match length in months, close reason (relocation, scheduling, mismatch, youth exited, unknown), mentor age band, and whether the mentor was a returning volunteer. Chapter-level attributes: paid staff FTE, urban/rural, 2024 training policy change (yes for 134 chapters). Known gap: 3 chapters in the Mountain region lack 2023 close reasons.

prompt:
I need the front end for Retain Lab Workbench. An analysis workspace used by a university nonprofit-studies research group to examine program data that partner nonprofits share under data-use agreements.

Who's using it: Dr. Hana Kowalczyk, a postdoctoral researcher in a public policy school's Nonprofit Effectiveness Lab. She is comfortable with statistics and has spent four months with this dataset, preparing findings for the partner organization's national board.

What they're doing right now: The partner, a national youth mentoring nonprofit, saw volunteer mentor retention drop from 71% to 58% in 2025, mostly in some regions. Hana's working hypothesis is that a 2024 cut to pre-match training hours lowered retention. A colleague thinks it's caused by longer waits between mentor sign-up and being matched with a child. She is breaking retention down by chapter, training hours, and wait-to-match days, picking out the chapters that don't fit either explanation, and deciding which pattern holds up well enough to present at Tuesday's lab meeting.

What's in the system at this point: 18,412 de-identified mentor records from 212 chapters across 9 regions, 2021–2025. Fields: chapter ID, region, chapter size, mentor sign-up date, training hours completed (range 2–14), days from sign-up to match (median 47, range 3–310), match start/end dates, match length in months, close reason (relocation, scheduling, mismatch, youth exited, unknown), mentor age band, and whether the mentor was a returning volunteer. Chapter-level attributes: paid staff FTE, urban/rural, 2024 training policy change (yes for 134 chapters). Known gap: 3 chapters in the Mountain region lack 2023 close reasons.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
